listening.instructionA: A. Listen to a radio programme about good manners adopted in four countries. What advice does the travel expert give to the four people? Tick (✓) the pieces of advice mentioned in the programme. The first one is done for you.
listening.instructionB: B. Listen again and circle the correct answers.

questions.prompt: According to the travel expert, you do not need to give a ‘wai’ to ______ in Thailand.
options: people who are older than you
people who are from lower social status than you

questions.prompt: The Japanese like ______ when they meet people for the first time.
In Japan, you should take off ______ first before entering someone’s house.
In Russia, leaving empty bottles on the dinner table is considered ______.
According to the travel expert, the Koreans are happy if they bow very ______.

speaking.instruction: C. In pairs, think of three examples of good manners and three examples of bad manners in your country. Then tell your examples to another pair of students.
D. Discuss the following question in groups. Then present your advice to the rest of the class using the useful language phrases in the box.
speaking.body:
• What advice would you give foreigners coming to live and work in your country?

Useful language
Giving advice
• You should + v-inf …
• You must / have to + v-inf …
• You can + v-inf …
• You need to + v-inf …
• Remember to + v-inf …
• The most important one / thing to remember is + to + v-inf …
• You shouldn’t + v-inf …
• You mustn’t + v-inf …
• You don’t + have to + v-inf …
• You can’t + v-inf …
• You don’t + need to + v-inf …
• The most important thing to remember is + not to + v-inf …

speaking.instruction: E. Work in pairs. Say whether the following manners (a–c) are good or bad in the situation given below. Give reasons.
speaking.body:
When you are invited to someone’s birthday party,
(a) bringing presents is …
(b) complaining about the food is …
(c) arriving more than fifteen minutes late is …
